Q1: Heptachlor exhibits significant known hazards, receiving Tier 1 ratings for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). It also shows endocrine disruption potential, categorized as Tier 2, indicating an expanded perspective on this hazard. The chemical currently has a data deficiency (Tier 4) regarding its inhalation hazards.
Q2: Heptachlor is featured on numerous prominent 'Lists of Concern,' reflecting widespread recognition of its hazards. These include California's Proposition 65 for cancer and reproductive harm, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) Group 2B as a possible human carcinogen, and designation as a Persistent Organic Pollutant (POP). It is also listed under federal regulations such as the Clean Water Act, EPA's Drinking Water Standards, and as a Hazardous Air Pollutant, in addition to being identified by The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) as a potential endocrine disruptor.
Q3: Heptachlor is a well-characterized chemical, supported by extensive scientific literature with over 9,800 references, which is significantly above average. It has a precisely defined molecular formula (C10H5Cl7) and is categorized as a 'Small Molecule,' indicating it is not an incompletely defined substance. Furthermore, its hazard profile is largely complete, with only one out of seven hazard classes identified as data deficient (Tier 4).
